jurisdiction.name: Spain
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Spain created Europe's first AI supervisory agency, AESIA, through the 2022 budget and start-ups laws and its 2023 statute, and ran an early AI Act sandbox under Royal Decree 817/2023, but it has not yet enacted a law implementing the EU AI Act: the AI governance bill lapsed when parliament was dissolved in October 2026. National policy rests on the 2024 AI Strategy (replacing the 2020 national AI strategy), the 2021 Charter of Digital Rights and AI advisory councils, with ministries and bodies adding their own AI documents (tax agency, national health system, education, labour, the judiciary's 2026 AI use rules). AI clauses also appear in general laws on equal treatment, platform workers, employment, customer service, justice and workers' information rights, and two 2026 statutes name equality bodies as AI Act fundamental-rights authorities. The data protection authority AEPD and AESIA are the main regulators, with AEPD guidance and decisions and AESIA's 16 AI Act guides; Catalonia, Andalusia, the Basque Country, Valencia and Madrid have their own AI strategies, frameworks or bodies.
lead_institutions: Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública (SEDIA)
Agencia Española de Supervisión de la Inteligencia Artificial (AESIA)
Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers national law, the national government and ministries, regulators, and the five largest regions. European Union and Council of Europe instruments are shown through the regional files. Spain's AI governance bill and two bills on deepfakes lapsed when parliament was dissolved in October 2026, so they are listed as leads rather than records. Not yet verified from the official text: one document, a Labour ministry guide. AI laws in Galicia and Extremadura were found but not reviewed because they fall outside the five regions covered.

instruments.summary: Approves the organic statute of AESIA, the State agency created under Ley 28/2022 to supervise AI in Spain, setting its legal regime, seat in A Coruña, governing bodies (Presidency, Consejo Rector, Dirección) and internal structure. The statute gives AESIA functions to supervise AI systems on the market (issuing non-binding reports until the future AI rules apply), issue mandatory reports on AI pilots and on the impact of AI systems used by the public sector (including bias-minimisation, transparency and accountability criteria), run certification and awareness work, and act as Spain's national supervisory authority anticipated by the then-proposed EU AI Act. The agency became operational on constitution of its Consejo Rector within three months of entry into force.

instruments.official_title: Anteproyecto de Ley para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial
instruments.english_title: Draft Law for the Good Use and Governance of Artificial Intelligence (preliminary draft, public hearing version)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública (Secretaría de Estado de Digitalización e Inteligencia Artificial)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Council of Ministers on 11 March 2025 under art. 26.4 of Ley 50/1997, with urgent processing (Referencia del Consejo de Ministros, 11 March 2025). Public hearing (audiencia pública) on the Ministry's portal from 18 to 26 March 2025, with the draft text and its impact report (MAIN) attached. Superseded by the Proyecto de Ley Orgánica para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial, approved by the Council of Ministers on 26 May 2026 and published in BOCG Congreso Serie A núm. 97-1 of 12 June 2026 (expedient 121/000096), which added a chapter on AI in the State public sector and dropped the annex on real-time remote biometric identification. That bill lapsed (Concluido – Caducado) on 6 October 2026 when the Cortes were dissolved by Real Decreto 806/2026 (BOE 6 October 2026); no Spanish AI Act implementing law had been enacted as of 11 October 2026 (see leads).
instruments.scope: Operators of AI systems in Spain under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; national competent authorities
instruments.summary: Preliminary draft law to adapt Spanish law to the EU AI Act: it designates the Secretaría de Estado de Digitalización e Inteligencia Artificial (through its Dirección General de IA) as notifying authority, AESIA as single point of contact and general market surveillance authority, and sectoral market surveillance authorities including the AEPD and regional data protection authorities (biometrics, law enforcement, migration), the Banco de España and CNMV (creditworthiness scoring), the DGSFP (life and health insurance pricing), the CGPJ (administration of justice) and the Junta Electoral Central (democratic processes). It sets a national sanctions regime classifying very serious, serious and minor infringements with fines up to EUR 35 million or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices, adds a right to provisional withdrawal from the Spanish market of AI systems causing serious incidents, and, in an annex, rules on authorising real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Spain's first official draft of its AI Act implementing and sanctions law.

instruments.summary: Spain's comprehensive anti-discrimination law, which lists artificial intelligence and mass data management among its fields of application. Article 23 requires public administrations, where technically feasible, to put in place mechanisms so that algorithms used in decision-making take into account bias minimisation, transparency and accountability (covering design and training data), to promote impact assessments of possible discriminatory bias, and to prioritise transparency and interpretability of algorithmic decisions; administrations and companies must promote ethical, trustworthy AI, and a quality seal for algorithms is to be promoted.

instruments.scope: Controllers and processors of personal data in Spain; digital rights of citizens and workers
instruments.summary: Spain's organic data protection law, which adapts and complements the GDPR and therefore governs the processing of personal data for training and using AI systems. It requires information about profiling and the right to object (art. 11), refers the rights relating to automated individual decisions, including profiling, to art. 22 GDPR (art. 18), and in Title X recognises digital rights such as privacy against digital monitoring at work and digital disconnection. It also sets the AEPD's powers and the sanctions regime.

Its final provisions amend consumer law so that traders must disclose when a price has been personalised through automated decision-making and the parameters used, and such personalisation may not raise prices in situations of urgency or need.

instruments.summary: Guidance (orientaciones) introducing the data protection issues raised when controllers and processors use AI agents, i.e. systems that use language models to pursue a goal by planning, using tools and acting autonomously. It describes agentic systems, analyses their vulnerabilities affecting personal data, GDPR compliance aspects and agent-specific threats, and lists measures controllers and processors can adopt, also noting agents' potential as a privacy-enhancing tool and for data protection by design.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First Spanish regulator guidance specifically on agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: Exactitud, idoneidad y calidad de los datos en tratamientos de datos personales con Inteligencia Artificial
instruments.english_title: Accuracy, suitability and quality of data in personal data processing with artificial intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD)
instruments.publisher_name: Spanish Data Protection Agency
instruments.current_status: Published 21 July 2026 per the AEPD guides feed; the 23-page document itself carries no date.
instruments.summary: AEPD analysis of how the GDPR accuracy principle relates to data quality in AI processing, holding that the two are not equivalent and must be read in light of the purpose and suitability of the processing. It argues accuracy can require properties such as precision, granularity and update frequency depending on the purpose, that non-personal data feeding a processing must also meet suitable quality requirements, and that controllers need objective metrics for the quality of outputs, especially when developing or evolving AI systems and models.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection authority guidance on data quality and accuracy for AI.
metadata_gaps: document itself undated; date from AEPD guides feed

instruments.current_status: Dated 7 October 2026 (8 pp.). Notes that Real Decreto 723/2026 of 9 September enters into force on 5 October 2026 (the royal decree itself is a BOE instrument outside this part).
instruments.summary: AEPD note on the position after Real Decreto 723/2026, which develops article 8.5 of the Workers' Statute and requires employers to inform each worker in writing of algorithmic or automated decision-making systems and, where they decide on working conditions, their rules and criteria. It stresses that this labour duty does not displace the GDPR and LOPDGDD (lawfulness, transparency, minimisation, accuracy, data protection by design, risk management, art. 22), and draws on the AEPD warning AI-00009-2026 on an AI tool for screening job candidates.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator guidance on algorithmic management and automated decisions at work.

instruments.issuing_authority: Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD), Director
instruments.publisher_name: Spanish Data Protection Agency
instruments.current_status: Individual enforcement decision binding on the addressee (not general guidance). Procedure opened 5 May 2021; proposed resolution 29 June 2021; voluntary payment 19 July 2021; the termination resolution is signed by the AEPD Director (Mar España Martí) but its exact date is not printed.
instruments.summary: Decision closing the AEPD sanctioning procedure against supermarket chain Mercadona over a facial recognition system deployed in its stores to detect people with final convictions or restraining orders. The proposed resolution found infringements of GDPR articles 6 and 9 (biometric data with no applicable exception), 5.1.c, 12-13, 25 and 35; Mercadona paid the reduced fine of EUR 2,520,000 on 19 July 2021 and was ordered to stop all facial recognition processing in its establishments (art. 58.2.f GDPR).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Landmark Spanish enforcement decision on biometric AI (live facial recognition) under the GDPR.
metadata_gaps: exact date of the termination resolution not printed (month inferred from the 19 July 2021 payment)

instruments.summary: Formal warning under GDPR article 58.2.a to a company planning to deploy a group-developed AI tool that analyses CVs, scores and prioritises candidates in recruitment and internal mobility. Before deployment the company must apply data protection by design and by default (arts. 24-25), assess risks and carry out a DPIA where high risk exists (art. 35), ensure transparency to candidates, and assess whether article 22 applies, ensuring that human intervention is effective and not merely formal.

instruments.summary: Box in the Banco de España's 2024 Supervision Report setting out its supervisory view of AI in banking: risks of bias and discrimination in credit and the explainability problem of 'black box' models, and the AI Act's high-risk requirements for credit scoring of natural persons. It states that, anticipating its designation as AI Act market surveillance authority for AI used in credit to natural persons, the Bank is preparing to supervise compliance, assess conformity, follow incidents and coordinate with AESIA, and has set up a cross-departmental AI working group that includes an internal governance model for ethical and responsible AI use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Banking supervisor's stated approach to AI Act market surveillance in credit.

instruments.official_title: Inteligencia Artificial y Competencia. Aportación conjunta de la Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia (CNMC) y la Autoritat Catalana de la Competència (ACCO)
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence and Competition: joint contribution of the CNMC and the Catalan Competition Authority (ACCO)
instruments.issuing_authority: Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia (CNMC) and Autoritat Catalana de la Competència (ACCO)
instruments.publisher_name: National Markets and Competition Commission
instruments.current_status: Undated 10-page document linked from the CNMC press note of 30 September 2020 (Madrid-Barcelona), which states the contribution was filed in the Commission consultation under reference F529843.
instruments.summary: Position paper submitted to the European Commission's consultation on the AI White Paper, on the competition challenges of AI and the digital economy (zero-price models, speed of digital markets, data mergers, algorithmic collusion). It proposes adapting the law so that competition authorities can use AI to detect illegal conduct and, in investigations, examine the code of the algorithms used and access electronic information, databases and applications, and calls for cooperation with other administrations, data protection authorities, research centres and universities.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Competition authority position on algorithmic collusion and AI-enabled enforcement.
metadata_gaps: document undated; date from the CNMC press note

instruments.official_title: Acord del Govern pel qual s'aprova l'Estratègia d'Intel·ligència Artificial de Catalunya
instruments.english_title: Government Agreement approving the Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Catalonia (Catalonia.AI)
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Catalonia (Govern de la Generalitat), on a proposal of the Department of Digital Policies and Public Administration with the Department of Business and Knowledge
instruments.publisher_name: Government of Catalonia
instruments.current_status: Approved at the Govern session of 18 February 2020 (diligence on the signed agreement, e-signed 20.02.2020; file SIG20PDA0059). Succeeded by the Estratègia Catalunya IA 2030 (Acord GOV/262/2025, 11 November 2025), which describes Catalonia.AI as the 2020 strategy born in a context that 'ja no és el mateix'; no express repeal was seen, so lifecycle is left as published.
instruments.summary: Government agreement of 18 February 2020 approving the Catalan AI Strategy (Catalonia.AI), which aims to make Catalonia a leading region in the development and implementation of ethical, people-centred AI, prioritising sectors such as agri-food, health, education, environment, mobility, tourism, culture, industry and public services. It is deployed through an action plan around six axes (ecosystem; research and innovation; talent; infrastructure and data; AI adoption; ethics and society), co-led by the Department of Digital Policies and Public Administration and the Department of Business and Knowledge.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional AI strategy of Catalonia.

instruments.official_title: Marc de gestió de riscos d'intel·ligència artificial de l'Administració de la Generalitat de Catalunya
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework of the Administration of the Generalitat de Catalunya
instruments.issuing_authority: Comissió d'Intel·ligència Artificial of the Generalitat de Catalunya; published by the Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació (CTTI)
instruments.publisher_name: Government of Catalonia
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Generalitat's AI Commission on 11 December 2024; version 2.0.0, last updated 12 May 2025 (cover page).
instruments.summary: Framework for identifying, assessing, controlling and monitoring the risks of AI systems used by the Generalitat de Catalunya administration and its public sector, set within the data-governance model under Decree 76/2020 on digital administration. It sets roles and responsibilities, a risk-management process across the AI lifecycle (holistic system understanding, risk level identification, estimation, control measures, monitoring and recovery plans) and governance principles, with an annex mapping lifecycle risks to control measures.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mandatory-in-practice AI risk framework for the Catalan regional administration.

instruments.official_title: Model per a l'AIDF: guia i casos d'ús. Metodologia aplicada de l'avaluació d'impacte sobre els drets fonamentals en el disseny i desenvolupament de la IA
instruments.english_title: FRIA Model: Guide and Use Cases. Applied methodology for fundamental rights impact assessment in the design and development of AI
instruments.issuing_authority: Catalan Data Protection Authority (APDCAT), 'DPD en xarxa' working group led by Prof. Alessandro Mantelero
instruments.publisher_name: Catalan Data Protection Authority
instruments.current_status: Guide dated 'Barcelona, 2025'; presented by APDCAT on 28 January 2025 (Data Protection Day), per search results for the APDCAT press note; exact day not printed in the PDF. APDCAT later released an 'Aplicació FRIA' software tool based on the model. The Basque Data Protection Authority signed an agreement with APDCAT (June 2025) to promote the model.
instruments.summary: APDCAT guide setting out a methodology for fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA/AIDF) of AI systems, linked to Article 27 of the EU AI Act and its interaction with data protection impact assessments. The model has three phases (planning and scoping, data collection and risk analysis using probability/exposure and severity matrices to build an impact index, and risk management), provides a template, and illustrates it with real use cases from bodies within APDCAT's remit.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional DPA methodology for AI Act fundamental rights impact assessments.

instruments.official_title: Acuerdo de 20 de junio de 2023, del Consejo de Gobierno, por el que se aprueba la Estrategia Andaluza de Inteligencia Artificial 2030
instruments.english_title: Agreement of 20 June 2023 of the Governing Council approving the Andalusian Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Consejo de Gobierno de la Junta de Andalucía (Consejería de la Presidencia, Interior, Diálogo Social y Simplificación Administrativa; drafted by the Agencia Digital de Andalucía)
instruments.publisher_name: Regional Government of Andalusia
instruments.current_status: Agreement adopted 20 June 2023; published BOJA no. 119, 23 June 2023, p. 10780/1 onwards. Agencia Digital de Andalucía transparency page lists it among current plans. Its formulation was approved by Acuerdo de 7 de febrero de 2022 (BOJA no. 28, 10 Feb 2022) as the 'Estrategia Andaluza de Inteligencia Artificial 2022-2025'; the strategy was finally approved with a 2030 horizon.
instruments.summary: Approves the Andalusian AI Strategy 2030, published in full in BOJA no. 119 of 23 June 2023, as the general planning instrument for AI policy in Andalusia aligned with Spanish and EU frameworks. It sets 4 challenges and 12 strategic objectives: placing Andalusia at the European forefront in AI use, improving business competitiveness, increasing trust in AI with the Administration leading by example, and fostering AI use within the Junta de Andalucía's administration.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional AI strategy of Andalusia.

instruments.official_title: Estrategia de Gobierno de la Inteligencia Artificial del Sector Público de la CAE
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Governance Strategy for the Public Sector of the Basque Autonomous Community
instruments.issuing_authority: Basque Government (Department of Governance, Digital Administration and Self-Government)
instruments.publisher_name: Basque Government
instruments.current_status: The PDF itself bears no approval date; the Basque Government's own published column by Councillor Maria Ubarretxena (bideoak2.euskadi.eus, 14 November 2025) states the strategy was 'aprobada el pasado 23 de octubre' (2025). Council of Government agreement not located.
instruments.summary: Strategy setting the governance model for adopting AI across the Basque public sector, grounded in the EU AI Act (prohibited practices, high-risk identification) and updating the 2024 Ethical Manifesto on data and AI governance with principles in six areas. It defines mission, vision and objectives, a governance model of agents and roles, project and demand management for AI adoption, technology provision, policies on AI risk management, lifecycle and data protection, an AI literacy and training plan, and an implementation timetable.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Basque public-sector AI governance strategy.

instruments.official_title: Ley 1/2022, de 13 de abril, de la Generalitat, de Transparencia y Buen Gobierno de la Comunitat Valenciana
instruments.english_title: Law 1/2022 of 13 April of the Generalitat on Transparency and Good Governance of the Valencian Community
instruments.issuing_authority: Les Corts Valencianes; promulgated by the President of the Generalitat
instruments.publisher_name: Generalitat Valenciana
instruments.current_status: Published in DOGV no. 9323 of 22 April 2022 (bilingual Valencian/Spanish; Valencian title 'Llei 1/2022, de 13 d'abril, de la Generalitat, de Transparència i Bon Govern de la Comunitat Valenciana'). Under final provision 3, chapter II of title I (active publicity, including art. 16.1(l)) entered into force twelve months after publication (April 2023); other provisions follow different rules. Consolidated text later amended (not reviewed).
instruments.summary: Valencian transparency and good-governance law. Article 16.1(l) requires the administrations within its scope to publish, as active publicity, the list of algorithmic or AI systems that have an impact on administrative procedures or the provision of public services, with an understandable description of their design and operation, their level of risk and a contact point, in line with transparency and explicability principles.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding algorithmic/AI transparency register obligation for Valencian administrations.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Catalonia (Govern de la Generalitat); Department of Business and Labour / digital policy area (Politiques Digitals)
instruments.publisher_name: Government of Catalonia
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Govern on 11 November 2025 (Acord GOV/262/2025) and published in DOGC no. 9541 of 13 November 2025, per the Generalitat's Portal Jurídic de Catalunya notice (24.11.2025). Scope: the Generalitat and the public and private sectors of Catalonia.
instruments.summary: Catalonia's AI strategy to 2030, approved by Government Agreement GOV/262/2025 (DOGC no. 9541, 13 November 2025), aiming to make AI a strategic asset for Catalonia's economic, social and territorial progress and a European reference for ethical, safe and democratic AI. It contains 88 actions in 8 axes (AI infrastructure; talent; research; AI in business; AI in the public sector; ethics, regulation and safeguards; digital society; global projection) built on five guiding principles, mobilising about EUR 1,000 million, and succeeds the 2020 Catalonia.AI strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current regional AI strategy of Catalonia.

instruments.issuing_authority: Consell de la Generalitat Valenciana (Conselleria de Innovación, Universidades, Ciencia y Sociedad Digital)
instruments.publisher_name: Generalitat Valenciana

instruments.english_title: Ethical Manifesto on the Governance of Data and Artificial Intelligence Systems of the Basque Public Sector
instruments.issuing_authority: Basque Government (Department of Governance, Digital Administration and Self-Government), as part of the Data Governance Strategy of the Basque public sector
instruments.publisher_name: Basque Government
instruments.current_status: Published as web pages on euskadi.eus. instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Basque public-sector AI ethics principles and algorithm-catalogue commitment.

instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional AI governance body for the Madrid administration.

instruments.english_title: AEPD warning AI-00009-2026 to a company planning an AI tool to screen and score job applications

instruments.publisher_name: Spanish Data Protection Agency
instruments.current_status: Warning (advertencia) under Article 58(2)(a) GDPR addressed to an anonymised controller and signed by the AEPD President. The warning prints no date; the AEPD press note dates it 23 September 2026.
instruments.summary: Prior warning under Article 58(2)(a) GDPR to an anonymised company that planned to introduce an AI tool to analyse CVs, score and rank candidates in recruitment and internal mobility. The AEPD tells the company to apply data protection by design and by default, assess the risks to candidates and staff and carry out a data protection impact assessment before use where the processing is high-risk, inform candidates clearly about the tool's role, and ensure that human intervention in the final decision is real and effective.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection regulator's preventive warning on AI screening of job applicants before deployment.

instruments.current_status: Warning (advertencia) under Article 58(2)(a) GDPR addressed to an anonymised controller and signed by the AEPD President. The warning prints no date; the AEPD press note dates it 6 October 2026.

instruments.official_title: Plan IA360: Plan para un despliegue responsable de la IA
instruments.english_title: IA360 Plan: a plan for the responsible deployment of AI
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidencia del Gobierno (La Moncloa)
instruments.publisher_name: Presidency of the Government of Spain (La Moncloa)
instruments.current_status: Presented by the President of the Government at the event 'IA360: Plan para un despliegue responsable de la IA' on 21 September 2026 (date as printed on the La Moncloa activity page, which hosts the 15-page plan PDF). The PDF itself prints no date. The plan describes itself as a roadmap of actions for the next 12 months; its milestones (for example a tripartite agreement on AI adoption, a post-quantum cryptography plan and a Royal Decree) are announcements, not adopted instruments.
instruments.summary: Government roadmap, presented by the President of the Government, to place Spain in the world top five in AI from a responsible and ethical approach. It sets out strategic projects across compute and models, business and talent adoption, security (including cybersecurity and post-quantum measures and monitoring of frontier models), a social pact on AI and work, administrative simplification and international alliances, with milestones dated from October 2026 to 2027.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Latest national AI policy plan, adding security, labour and adoption measures to the 2024 AI Strategy; it creates no binding obligations.
instruments.evidence_reference: esp-sweep-2026-10-23. Publication date source: La Moncloa activity page 'Pedro Sánchez anuncia el Plan IA360...' dated 21.9.2026; PDF undated.

leads.title: Proyecto de Ley Orgánica para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial (121/000096)
leads.english_title: Organic Bill for the Good Use and Governance of Artificial Intelligence
leads.issuing_authority: Gobierno (Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública); Congreso de los Diputados
leads.note: Approved by the Council of Ministers on 26 May 2026 (Referencia del Consejo de Ministros) and published in BOCG Congreso Serie A núm. 97-1 of 12 June 2026 (https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CONG/BOCG/A/BOCG-15-A-97-1.PDF). Designates the AI Act notifying authority, AESIA as single point of contact and market surveillance authorities, regulates sandbox governance and AI in the State public sector (inventory of AI systems, AI delegate per entity), complaints, whistleblower protection and the sanctions regime (arts. 1-41). Committee: Economía, Comercio y Transformación Digital; amendment period extended to 7 October 2026. Congreso record: 'Concluido – (Caducado)' from 6 October 2026, i.e. lapsed on dissolution of the Cortes by Real Decreto 806/2026 (BOE 6 October 2026). Not enacted; Spain has no AI Act implementing/sanctions law as of 11 October 2026. A future Government would have to re-submit it.

leads.title: Proyecto de Ley Orgánica para la protección de las personas menores de edad en los entornos digitales (121/000052)
leads.english_title: Organic Bill for the protection of minors in digital environments
leads.issuing_authority: Gobierno; Congreso de los Diputados (Comisión de Justicia)
leads.note: BOCG Congreso Serie A núm. 52-1 of 11 April 2025 (https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CONG/BOCG/A/BOCG-15-A-52-1.PDF). Would add art. 173 bis to the Criminal Code punishing the dissemination, without consent, of realistic images or voice recordings generated, modified or recreated with automated systems, algorithms or AI ('ultrafalsificaciones'/sexual or degrading deepfakes). Urgent procedure; amendment to the whole rejected 11 September 2025; at report stage (ponencia) from 27 November 2025. Congreso record: 'Concluido – (Caducado)' from 6 October 2026 (dissolution). Not enacted.

leads.title: Proyecto de Ley Orgánica de protección civil de los derechos al honor, a la intimidad personal y familiar y a la propia imagen (121/000103)
leads.english_title: Organic Bill on civil protection of the rights to honour, personal and family privacy and one's own image
leads.issuing_authority: Gobierno (Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes); Congreso de los Diputados (Comisión Constitucional)
leads.note: Anteproyecto approved by the Council of Ministers on 13 January 2026; bill published in BOCG Congreso Serie A núm. 104-1 of 27 July 2026 (https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CONG/BOCG/A/BOCG-15-A-104-1.PDF). Would make unlawful the dissemination or use of a person's image or voice created, simulated or technologically manipulated to look extremely realistic (deepfakes, referring to the AI Act definition) and unauthorised commercial use of image or voice. Congreso record: 'Concluido – (Caducado)' from 6 October 2026 (dissolution). Not enacted. No official public-hearing text of the anteproyecto was found on the Justice ministry's site.
